title: Split policy graph and speed up regional evaluation pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The smart routing layer currently evaluates the full policy graph for every request which couples regional decision logic, policy predicates, and fallback scoring into a single hotpath. This has led to high tail latency under surge, duplicated evaluation code across region adapters, and difficulty landing non-blocking kernel/serialization upgrades. Goal: Reduce CPU and lock contention during route evaluation by decomposing the monolithic policy graph into a two-stage pipeline: a lightweight route prefilter (fast, local checks and affinity) and an extensible policy executor (heavyweight scoring, fallback orchestration) that can run asynchronously with bounded backpressure. This ticket covers design, incremental implementation, and rollout strategy for the split while preserving correctness and observability.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end request path executes prefilter + policy executor with no behavioral regressions on 99% of traffic
P50 route evaluation latency reduced by at least 30% in staging under representative load
Lock contention metrics (contention_ms per request) drop by >= 40% on routing hotpaths
Canary rollout plan validated: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on SLA violations
Comprehensive unit and integration tests for prefilter rules and executor fallbacks are added
Telemetry: new span tags and metrics for prefilter hits, executor queue depth, and fallback decisions are visible in Console
plan: Design doc (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/routing/split-policy-prefilter) reviewed by infra and runtime
Introduce prefilter interface and adapters behind a feature flag; add benchmarks
Implement asynchronous policy executor with bounded work queue and prioritized processing for high-SLA tenants
Gradually migrate regional adapters to call prefilter first; keep legacy path behind flag
Add observability hooks: tracing spans, counters for prefilter pass/fail, executor queue latency
Canary rollout with synthetic load and real traffic gating; iterate on thresholds and backpressure behavior
Deprecate legacy monolithic evaluator once rollout passes canary and reliability checks
risks: Behavioral drift: subtle policy ordering differences may change routing outcomes for edge tenants
Backpressure misconfiguration could increase p99 latency if executor queues grow without proper shedding
Incompatibility with some dedicated/private adapters that rely on side-effectful policy predicates
Telemetry gaps during migration could make regressions hard to detect if not instrumented correctly
qa_notes: Prepare a set of deterministic request traces used by routing regression suite
Run controlled canary with production-like traffic profiles using canary-job in infra cluster
Create smoke dashboards: prefilter hit-rate, executor queue depth, avg evaluation time, fallback counts
Validate fallback correctness by replaying incident traces recorded in incidents-dashboard
